evidence: The original SKILL.md said each primitive 'maps to `reactive_graph`' while the doc's Open questions leaves reactive_graph vs own runtime undecided, and the skill's own charter says it never holds the doc's reasoning. 2598982 replaced the table with a pointer.
guidance_note: When writing a companion skill that defers to a design doc, check every paragraph for facts copied from the doc before the first push, and replace each one with a pointer to the doc section.

evidence: The agent confirmed the workflow 'lives in the maintainer's global instructions, not this repo's CLAUDE.md', so attributing it to CLAUDE.md was false. 2598982 restates it as the skill's own rule.
guidance_note: Before attributing a rule to a named file, open that file and find the rule there. Global instructions are not the repo's CLAUDE.md.

evidence: 2598982 did not touch the Phase 0 line, so the paraphrase was there from the start. But it is the same restated-doc-fact gap F1 named, and the F1 fix removed only the reactive-runtime instance. The paraphrase dropped the 'appended to docs/daemon-memory-2026-09.md' half of the doc's exit criterion.
guidance_note: When a finding says the skill restates the doc, sweep the whole skill for every restated doc fact (exit criteria, Done, citations) in the same fix, not just the flagged section.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 2598982 changed only SKILL.md, and the RUST-PORT.md line 'set (to / from / min-max-by / int / cycle / persist dual)' was in the original commit. Listing the dual form as a sixth value source contradicts the doc's own 'five value sources'.
guidance_note: When a doc enumerates arms of a TS union, copy the list from the type definition and say where it came from, rather than summarizing from memory.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the citation of `What the landscape shows` was in the original SKILL.md line 37, which 2598982 did not change. The agent agreed that only Template engine carries the no-crate-fits reasoning, and the Template engine section in the packet holds that argument.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the `gotmpl` crate name in the Component map was in the original doc, and 48b4e66 did not touch it. The same doc evaluates and rejects the published `gotmpl` 0.6.1, so reusing the name is self-contradictory.
guidance_note: When naming a new crate, check the name against the crates the same document surveys and against crates.io.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 48b4e66 did not touch either line. 'checked before phase 1' in Why Rust and 'verified and pinned' as a Phase 1 exit criterion were both in the original doc, and they disagree on timing.
guidance_note: When a doc states a timing or gate in two places, keep one statement and point to it from the other.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the cache row with `session-state.ts` inheriting the `src/daemon/cache/` prefix was in the original doc. The Reactive runtime row gives `src/daemon/session-state.ts`, so the shorthand pointed at the wrong directory.

evidence: The Done section existed from the start, but the reviewer says it is 'exactly the anti-pattern the author already fixed at line 57'. The F3 fix pointed Phase 0 at Sequencing and left the Done paraphrase, which diverged from the Phase 4 exit. b8e22c3 moved the extra criterion into the doc and pointed Done at it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the 'Snapshot file' header was in the original doc, and b8e22c3 did not touch it. Every cell under it holds an MB size, so the header was wrong; 7a89217 renamed it.

The flag is a false positive: the 'satisfies all six primitives' sentence was in the original doc. reactive_graph's own table row marks batch 'partial' and zero-observer caching 'not stated', so the summary overclaimed.
guidance_note: When a summary sentence draws on a comparison table, check it against the table's caveat cells before writing 'all'.

evidence: 48b4e66, the F4 fix, rewrote this exact line as 'set (...), copy, open, doctor; plus the dual set+persist form' without reading action.ts. The union also has persist, the structural edits, reset, undo, and redo, so the rewritten list was still incomplete and drew another finding.
guidance_note: When fixing an enumeration of a TS union, open the union's definition and rebuild the list from it rather than editing the flagged item.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: '`untracked` at a few sites' was in the original doc, and 7a89217 did not touch it. The agent's grep found no mobx `untracked` import in the three files, so the doc's six-primitive framing was wrong from the first commit.
guidance_note: Derive a dependency's usage list from a grep of the actual imports at writing time, and cite the grep; don't list primitives from memory.

narrative: This is a docs-only PR (a design doc plus a skill), and the reviewer drip-fed pre-existing inaccuracies across five rounds before hitting the round cap. Most ON-NAMED-FIX flags are false positives: the flagged lines predate the fix commits. Two real chains exist. The F1 'skill restates the doc' fix was not swept across the skill, which produced F3 and then F9. The F4 enumeration fix rewrote the ActionDecl line without reading action.ts, which produced F12. Every round would still have happened on the pre-existing findings, so none is avoidable through better fixes alone.
guidance_observations: The original doc had many unverified factual claims (an untracked usage, a crate name collision, wrong path prefixes, column headers); a claim-by-claim check against the source before the first push would have cut most of the rounds.
Fixes were accepted narrowly, item by item; each of the two recurring classes (restated doc facts, hand-enumerated union arms) needed one sweep, not one fix per finding.
Five rounds hit MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS, so the final commit 4524779 went unreviewed.

evidence: The test hardcoded `/^✕/` while the file already imported DISCLOSURE_CLOSED from the module that exports DISCLOSURE_GLYPH_CLOSE. 1435da0 asserts the prefix against the constant.
guidance_note: When a test asserts a glyph, import the exported constant the production code uses rather than retyping the literal.

evidence: The original code appended `...closeLead` to the sink whenever the body was open, even when renderBody returned no lines. The agent's point holds: gating on `bodyLines.length > 0` would still sink one ✕ when N rows were led. 1435da0 folds the sink from `bodyLines.flatMap(leadOf)`, the same list the lead was applied to, and a test pins the empty body.
guidance_note: When a side channel (the sink) records what the main output laid, derive it from the same list the output was built from, not from a separate predicate.

evidence: In the original composeBlocks, the horizontal arm put `lead` only on row0, and `drops` (which include a multi-line segment's continuation lines) got none, so those rows were led zero times. The agent found the wider case (a v inside an h) and replaced the threaded lead with a per-line `band` tag, led at one site. Tests pin five body rows each led once.
guidance_note: Before threading a per-row decoration down a tree walk, write the table of every line shape (row0, continuation line, nested-v row, menu drop) and decide which band each belongs to.

evidence: The 'new pattern' premise is wrong: the original code already spread the same `lead` array into every row (`[...lead, ...]` in composeBlocks, `[...ctx.lead, ...]` per inline line). Whether FlexStrip mutates cells cannot be checked from the packet; the reviewer itself says it is unverified, and the agent's no-mutation claim plus its width-40 byte-identical render is not shown. The cited law is about null guards, not defensive copies.

The flag is a false positive: the two separate checks (`toMatch(/^✕/)` plus `toContain("✗ tmux truecolor")`) were in the original commit, and 1435da0 only swapped the literal for the constant. The ✕ is its own cell under powerline style, so a joiner glyph sits between it and the report text. The reviewer's proposed `^✕✗ tmux truecolor` regex would fail on the real row.

The comment 'Built only when there is a body to lead (a closed body has no rows)' predates the review. F2 named the open-but-empty body case, and the F2 fix corrected the sink but left this comment, which assumes an open body has rows. The agent accepted, but its fix a58a9d7 was held unpushed (see F9).
guidance_note: When a finding names an edge case (an open body with no rows), grep the surrounding comments for statements that assume it away and fix them in the same commit.

evidence: `expectLedBy`'s `otherCloses` filters on `closes(l, key)` only, so the comment's 'no other disclosure's ✕ may sit anywhere on the row' overclaims. Narrowing the comment was one of the reviewer's two options, and the agent's reason against tightening (an open `(?)` trigger's own ✕ may legitimately sit on the row) holds. The fix a58a9d7 was never pushed.
guidance_note: Write a test helper's doc comment from what the predicate filters on, not from what the helper is meant to guard.

evidence: The round-2 diff hunk still shows the original 'no other disclosure's ✕ may sit anywhere' wording. The F7 fix, a58a9d7, was 'held at the maintainer's request' and never landed, and the only later commit, cc0e03e, touches pricing.json alone. The PR merged at 00:37 before this 00:40 review, and the thread was never answered.
guidance_note: A fix reply must name a commit that is on the remote branch. Before merging, check that every held commit named in a thread was pushed.

evidence: The stale 'Built only when there is a body to lead' comment is still in the round-2 hunk because the F6 fix, a58a9d7, was held unpushed. The PR merged before this review posted, so the defect shipped and the thread is unresolved.
guidance_note: Don't resolve a thread on an unpushed commit; land the commit with the next push or leave the thread open.

narrative: The agent turned two round-0 edge-case findings (a phantom sink ✕, unled continuation rows) into one structural fix, a per-line band tag, which is well reasoned and tested. Its round-1 pushbacks on cell sharing and test contiguity rest on checkable reasons, though FlexStrip immutability cannot be confirmed from the packet. It accepted two round-1 comment fixes but held them in an unpushed commit, a58a9d7, which never landed. Round 2 re-raised both, and the PR merged before that review finished, so the stale comments shipped.
guidance_observations: A held-back fix commit is invisible to the reviewer and to merge; replying 'committed as <sha>, push held' and resolving the thread let two accepted fixes vanish.
The merge happened while a review round was still running, so its findings arrived on an already-merged PR.

evidence: The PR edited the line above (☰ → 🍫) and left the next line's `menus.settings_presets.…`, which the reviewer says should be `menus.settings_pickers` (PICKER_KEY shared by all picker controls). The agent agreed, and 647ef2b names the right key; the packet does not show settings-menu.ts.
guidance_note: When editing one line of a comment, re-verify every identifier in the whole comment block against the current code.

narrative: This was a large PR with one trivial stale-identifier finding in round 0, fixed directly. Rounds 1 and 2 hit the token cap: each reviewed only a few scopes and found nothing. src/config, docs, and test were never fully reviewed in any round.
guidance_observations: Every round hit the token cap, so much of the 50-file diff (src/config, docs) was never reviewed; the clean rounds are not evidence the PR was clean.

evidence: The PR switched the open door glyph from DISCLOSURE_GLYPH_CLOSE to DOOR_CLOSE_GLYPH, while menuGlyphSpec still refused only ✕, so `menuGlyph: "❌"` would make the closed and open states identical. Replacing the rule rather than adding a second was one of the reviewer's options, and the agent's reason (✕ was refused only as the open glyph) is sound.
guidance_note: When swapping a constant a trigger uses, grep for every validator and message that names the old constant and move them with it.

evidence: The RenderedLine doc still said the trigger 'returns every line as `deeper`', while the PR's new inline placement keeps bodyHead as `own`/`span: "row"`. CLAUDE.md got the exception and the type's comment did not.
guidance_note: When adding an exception to an invariant, grep for every place the invariant is stated (type docs and CLAUDE.md) and update them together.

evidence: The merged `test.each` asserted only the banner, though the describe title promises the content is hidden. The agent also caught that the reviewer's `not.toContain("d")` would be vacuous ('d' appears in 'gated customized') and used a distinctive GATED_CONTENT template.
guidance_note: When collapsing tests into a test.each, check that every fact in the describe title still has an assertion.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 98cf652 touched only node-registry.ts, and the carry-up removal is the PR's own intentional change (the reviewer says so). The risk that someone re-adds the carry-up is real, but the d3f4c43 test asserts the banner and door render under a `{{ false }}` gate, so a re-add fails a test. The repo's no-new-comments rule is the agent's claim and is not visible in the packet.

The flag is a false positive for fix causation: 98cf652 changed only node-registry.ts. The drift comes from the PR's own removal of mapOpens from expandAnchor, which left mapOpens's doc naming 'the settings anchor's expansion'. 6bb92e7 deletes the clause.
guidance_note: When removing a call site, grep the callee's doc comment for a list of callers and update it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 6bb92e7 only edited the mapOpens comment, and the prependAnchor vertical-gated branch is the PR's original logic. No test built a gated vertical first child. b802527 adds one, and the agent reports it fails when the vertical arm is collapsed into the horizontal one.
guidance_note: When a function's comment names distinct cases, write one test per named case before pushing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: b802527 only added a settings-menu test, and the `Placement` type predates it. That 'inline' claims horizontal siblings is non-obvious, but per F8's quote, composeBlocks' own comment already states 'replaces its horizontal siblings whole', so the meaning has one home. A second prose copy beside the type is optional.

The flag is a false positive: b802527 touched settings-menu.test.ts, not disclosure-close.test.ts. The chain test after close asserted only one line and a first link of DOOR_GLYPH, which would not catch a stale `span: "row"` hiding the siblings. 34ba5a3 asserts that the closed bar text is reproduced and is mutation-checked.
guidance_note: For a reversible state (open/close), assert that the after-close output equals the before-open output, not only that it has the right shape.

narrative: There were eight rounds: two cancelled by newer pushes and one stopped at the round cap. Each review round found new pre-existing gaps in the PR's own change (a validator and comments that drifted from the glyph and placement changes, missing tests for named cases), not regressions from fixes. Most ON-NAMED-FIX/POST-REVIEW flags are false positives where the fix commit touched unrelated files. Both pushbacks (comment requests) were reasonable given tests or an existing comment that already pin the behavior.
guidance_observations: Most findings were drift the PR created against its own invariants (menuGlyphSpec, RenderedLine doc, mapOpens doc); a grep for each changed constant and invariant before the first push would have collapsed several rounds.
Test gaps for cases the code's own comments enumerate (gated stack, close reversibility) were found one per round; writing one test per named case up front would have avoided that.
